statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across public landing, listing, login, FAQ, 404 and one localized listing. Authenticated upload/profile/account surfaces were not covered because no test credentials were supplied.

page.framework: Server-rendered MPA with legacy Bootstrap/jQuery-style client enhancements
page.notes: Public adult media-sharing site. The origin was intermittent: one screenshot and sitemap request returned 503 while subsequent DOM and evidence captures succeeded.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and several controls are too short for comfortable touch use.
findings.evidence: The login focus probe reported outline:none and no box shadow for navigation links, the menu button, password field, submit button and footer links; several controls are 13–34px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add clear :focus-visible rings and increase interactive target boxes/spacing to at least 24px minimum, preferably 44px for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Explore can load slowly under lab conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 4.7s, Speed Index 16.4s and a 10.53s root-document response, despite a separate trace measuring LCP 1.53s; the variance itself indicates unreliable delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Stabilize origin response time, prioritize the LCP thumbnail, and monitor field LCP/INP/CLS by route.

findings.summary: Some images and the CAPTCHA input lack accessible alternatives or labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found two missing-alt images in the disclaimer; DOM inspection found the required captcha input has no associated label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images alt text, mark decorative imagery alt="", and associate a visible label/instructions with the CAPTCHA control.

findings.summary: Keyboard users cannot reliably see focus, and the login page lacks a semantic heading.
findings.evidence: Focus probing found no visible outline on most links/buttons/inputs, while the login DOM visually says Login but exposes no H1/H2/H3.
findings.suggestedFix: Add :focus-visible styling and use a real heading plus main landmark for the login content.

findings.summary: Locale indexing signals point English and default users at development hosts, and the sitemap was unavailable.
findings.evidence: The live page declares x-default and en hreflang as https://dev.erome.com/explore; /sitemap.xml returned 503 during recon while robots allows the public site.
findings.suggestedFix: Point hreflang entries at production canonical hosts, add reciprocal alternates, and keep sitemap.xml reliably available.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers show no CSP or nosniff; both Google Analytics cookies were set without Secure and all four cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP and nosniff, mark HTTPS cookies Secure, and use Lax/Strict SameSite unless cross-site behavior is required.

findings.summary: The page exposes a broad advertising and analytics network surface.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture saw 31 non-page origins, including Google Tag Manager/Analytics plus ad-provider and tsyndicate requests; analytics cookies persist for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory every third party, remove nonessential trackers, gate advertising/analytics appropriately, and shorten retention.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response lacks clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy in addition to CSP; only HSTS is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, a strict Referrer-Policy, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and CSP.

findings.summary: Prominent advertising links are styled as first-party navigation without being identified as ads.
findings.evidence: The first mobile row presents CAM GIRLS, AI CUM SLUT and AI JERK OFF as site chrome; DOM shows these route through /o/menu-* advertising redirects with no ad label.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label sponsored/external destinations and visually separate them from primary product navigation.

findings.summary: Transient and modal UI is built from generic divs instead of modern semantic primitives.
findings.evidence: Rendered DOM contains a Bootstrap-style div.modal with role=dialog and no dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate modal flows to <dialog> and transient menus to popover with declarative light-dismiss and focus handling.

findings.summary: Caching and render-critical delivery leave avoidable load cost.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported about 110KiB cache-lifetime savings and 310ms render-blocking savings; the HAR captured 58 requests and 759,455 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set durable immutable caching for versioned assets and trim confirmed render-blocking CSS/script chains.

findings.summary: The listing ships substantial unused and legacy code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 213KiB unused JavaScript, 31KiB unused CSS and 43KiB legacy JavaScript savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route bundles, remove unused library features, and serve a modern baseline bundle without unnecessary legacy transforms.

findings.summary: Many images omit intrinsic dimensions and responsive sources.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 18 images without width/height and 22 without srcset; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height for every image and provide responsive candidates for content thumbnails and avatars.

findings.summary: Deprecated unload handling prevents clean browser lifecycle behavior.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found an unload listener in libraries.js and four BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload listeners, use pagehide/visibilitychange where needed, and resolve the reported BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Public content pages lack social preview and structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The Explore DOM probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks despite a public media listing with named content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph/Twitter metadata and appropriate schema.org JSON-LD that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Localized pages are not built to adapt cleanly to bidirectional writing modes.
findings.evidence: The English page advertises 16 localized alternates and Spanish correctly uses lang=es, but stylesheet inspection counted 313 left, 214 right and zero logical-property declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace directional layout declarations with inline/block logical properties and test an RTL locale before adding one.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit standard autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: The required email and password inputs both expose an empty autocomplete value.
findings.suggestedFix: Add autocomplete="username" to email and autocomplete="current-password" to password; retain paste support.

findings.summary: The image-heavy feed does not use modern responsive image delivery consistently.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 41 legacy-format images, no modern-format images, and 22 missing srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and sizes/srcset candidates while keeping legacy fallback sources.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics consume a disproportionate share of the lightweight listing shell.
findings.evidence: The page contacted 31 non-page origins and known trackers during a 759KB load before the user opened any media.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, defer nonessential ad/analytics work until appropriate, and remove vendors that do not justify their cost.

findings.summary: The interface does not adapt its theme to the user’s color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are byte-identical, and the CSS probe found no color-scheme declaration or prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use preference-aware surface tokens so the theme follows the user without breaking the existing dark presentation.

findings.summary: Route and state changes use abrupt swaps rather than View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The full stylesheet probe found no view-transition rules; the public listing navigates with ordinary full-page anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-document and cross-document navigation with View Transitions, retaining the current instant fallback.

findings.summary: The long feed has no scroll-position feedback or state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The 5,016px mobile listing keeps static chrome and exposes no scroll-state/container or progress signal in the stylesheet probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header treatment for the long Explore feed.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays use legacy manual positioning rather than anchored positioning.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules, while navigation is implemented as custom/legacy menu chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with fallback positions for menus that must remain attached near viewport edges.

findings.summary: Responsive components rely only on viewport styling rather than container-aware behavior.
findings.evidence: The Explore stylesheet probe found no @container rules even though reusable feed cards and navigation appear at several widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable feed/card regions while keeping viewport rules as fallback where needed.

findings.summary: The app-like feed advertises installability but has no offline runtime.
findings.evidence: A valid standalone manifest is present, but navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration() returned null.
findings.suggestedFix: If installability is intentional, register a service worker with a small offline fallback; otherwise avoid presenting an incomplete app posture.
